title: circuit-interference-and-staggered-failover-postmortem
creator: Ava Chen
summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a multi-region degradation where overlapping circuit break thresholds and immediate failover logic caused a cascade of cold-cache tail latency and a sustained SLO miss on p99 latency and error rate for conversational generation routes.
timeline: 2026-03-09 10:12 UTC - First elevated error rates observed on primary region (us-west-2) for /v1/generate-chat route (alert: route-error-rate > 0.5%).

2026-03-09 10:14 UTC - Primary region circuit broker (per-cluster) opened due to combined load and short-window request spikes; automatic failover policy routed 35% of traffic to secondary region (eu-west-1).

2026-03-09 10:16 UTC - Secondary region experienced surging p99 latency as KV cache was cold and batching profiles mismatched expected sequence lengths; error rate increased and its circuit opened as well, triggering additional failback attempts and oscillation.

2026-03-09 10:20 UTC - Global routing attempted to route traffic to tertiary fallback models; routing selectors evaluated circuits independently leading to traffic split across regions with inconsistent capacity, creating uneven queueing and sustained p99 spikes.
2026-03-09 10:30 UTC - On-call rotated: manual intervention increased dedicated pool capacity in eu-west-1 and disabled immediate cross-region cutoff to stabilize traffic.
2026-03-09 11:05 UTC - Tail latency began trending down after warming caches and applying temporary batching profile override.
2026-03-09 12:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; incident review started same day and deep dive assigned.
2026-03-11 15:00 UTC - Postmortem draft circulated to SRE, runtime, and routing teams for feedback.
impact: Sustained SLO violation for 48-minute window. p99 latency for /v1/generate-chat rose from 520ms baseline to 2.8s peak in affected tenants; error rate across the route peaked at 1.9% (SLO target 0.5%). Two enterprise customers reported user-facing timeouts and opened support tickets.
detection: Automated SLO guardrails and route-error alerts fired from dashboard-runbook. The initial signal was an aggregated route-level increase in 5xxs and timeouts; internal synthetic checks for top customers also failed within minutes.
root_cause: A combination of factors produced the degradation:
root_cause_details: 1) Circuit hysteresis and threshold configuration: per-cluster circuit breakers were configured with overlapping short windows and identical thresholds. When the primary opened, the secondary received immediate extra traffic which tripped its own short-window breaker before caches and batching adjusted.

2) Coupled circuit evaluations: routing logic evaluated circuit state independently per region without global coordination, enabling oscillation and split traffic that exceeded regional warm-up capacity.

3) Cold KV caches + batching mismatch: failover traffic had different sequence-length distribution; batching kernels and cached prefixes were not pre-warmed in the secondary region, causing increased decode time per token and higher tail latency.
4) Monitoring blind spot: there was insufficient pre-failover synthetic coverage for the new batching profile introduced in runtime-1.22, so early signs of mismatch were missed.

5) Fall-through routing behavior: fallback policy attempted to route to less-compatible model variants without partial degradation modes (e.g., lower max tokens or quantized variants), which increased error rates.
short_term_mitigation: During the incident we performed three immediate actions to stop the cascade:
short_term_mitigation_list: A) Increased dedicated GPU pool size in eu-west-1 by 25% to absorb failover traffic (manual scale-up).
B) Temporarily disabled cross-region immediate cutoff so circuits used a staggered allowance instead of binary open/closed for 20 minutes.
C) Applied a temporary batching profile override in the runtime to align secondary region kernels with observed sequence lengths for the failing routes.
D) Warmed KV caches via controlled replays of hot prefixes for highest-traffic customers.
E) Communication: Sent status updates to affected customers and created support tickets for two enterprise customers; Customer Success handled active mitigation updates.
long_term_fixes: 1) Implement quorum-based circuit evaluation: require a two-step consensus (local + global) before triggering cross-region full failover to avoid simultaneous tripping (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-04-04).
2) Per-route staggered failover policy: allow percentage-based ramp with hysteresis windows tied to cache-warmup signals (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-11).

3) Dynamic pre-warming: when a region starts receiving >15% incremental traffic within 2 minutes, trigger automatic KV prefix pre-warm jobs and temporary batching profile alignment (owner: Data Plane team, due: 2026-04-18).

4) Improve synthetic coverage: add synthetic tests for new batching profiles and top-20 enterprise prompts across regions; integrate into pre-release CI for runtime-1.22+ (owner: QA SRE, due: 2026-03-28).
5) Route-aware fallback variants: build partial-degradation model variants and routing hints (max_tokens/quantized) to handle capacity shortages gracefully (owner: Model Serving, due: 2026-05-02).
6) Telemetry and dashboards: add a 'failover warmup index' metric and dashboard with per-region cache-hit, batch-size, and circuit-age visualizations (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-31).
7) Post-deploy canary validation: extend canary window for runtime and batching profile changes with automatic rollback thresholds tied to synthetic p99 tests (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-25).

postmortem_notes: Key lesson: failover logic must respect warmup characteristics of the serving runtime. Binary circuit open/closed semantics worked against us when combined with cold caches and newly-introduced batching profiles. We need to treat 'available capacity' as a multi-dimensional signal (cache-hit rate, queue depth, batch-size medians), not a single threshold.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz): emphasize customer communication in next incident playbook iterations and add a customer-impact severity mapping to the alert templates.
Design (Theo Marquez): suggest UX for per-route staggered failover controls and clearer labels for 'warmup' signals in the Console.
SRE (Ravi Kapoor): require automated emergency runbook step to flip to 'stagger' mode instead of full cutover when downstream metrics indicate low cache-hit density.
next_steps: Track action items as individual Linear tickets (ENG-55235..ENG-55242). Re-run postmortem review after first chaos test and update runbooks and alerting thresholds based on measured warmup times.
contributor_comments: Miguel Torres: We underweighted cache-warmup in our failover SLO model; prototype quorum-based evaluation to reduce oscillation.
Ava Chen: Recommend adding a 'canary warmup' phase to release pipelines that triggers synthetic warmup traffic to secondary regions when rollout % > 10%.
Priya Nair: Will scope Console UX for staggered failover in next design sprint; needs collaboration with Observability for warmup signals.
